q: What is the youngest age at which you can take the Ohio knowledge test and get a temporary permit (TIPIC)?
exp: Ohio lets you take the vision screening and knowledge test, and then buy a TIPIC, at 15 and a half.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 1, p. 1 to 2; Ohio Revised Code 4507.05 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: How many questions are on the Ohio knowledge test, and what score do you need to pass?
exp: The test has 40 multiple choice questions and you need 75 percent, which is 30 correct.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 1, p. 1; BMV, Driver License and ID Cards (ohiobmv.gov/dl-gdl.aspx)

q: After you pass the knowledge test, how long do you have to buy your TIPIC at a Deputy Registrar?
exp: If you do not buy the TIPIC within 60 days, you must take the vision screening and knowledge test again.

q: You are 16 and hold a TIPIC. Who may supervise you from the front passenger seat at 4 p.m.?
exp: From 16 on, any licensed driver at least 21 may sit beside you, except between midnight and 6 a.m.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 1, p. 2; Ohio Revised Code 4507.05 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: A 17-year-old TIPIC holder wants to drive at 12:30 a.m. Who may supervise?
b: A licensed parent, guardian or custodian
d: No one; permit holders may never drive then
exp: From midnight to 6 a.m., a permit driver under 18 needs a licensed parent, guardian or custodian beside them (or an adult named on a notarized BMV 2438).
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 1, p. 2; BMV, Driver License and ID Cards (ohiobmv.gov/dl-gdl.aspx)

q: How many hours of supervised driving must a driver under 21 log in Ohio before the driving test?
a: 40 hours, with at least 10 at night
b: 50 hours, with at least 15 at night
c: 50 hours, with at least 10 at night
d: 65 hours, with at least 10 at night
exp: Ohio requires 50 logged hours, including at least 10 at night, certified on form BMV 5791.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 1, p. 3; Ohio Revised Code 4507.21 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: What driver education must a new driver under 21 complete in Ohio?
a: 30 hours of class and 6 hours of driving
b: 24 hours of class and 4 hours of driving
c: 8 hours of class and 24 hours of driving
d: 24 hours of class or online lessons and 8 hours of driving with an instructor
exp: Ohio driver education is 24 hours of classroom or online instruction plus 8 hours behind the wheel at a licensed school.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 1, p. 3; BMV, Driver License and ID Cards (ohiobmv.gov/dl-gdl.aspx)

q: How long must a driver under 18 hold a TIPIC before taking the driving test?
exp: Under 18, you must hold the TIPIC at least six months, even if your 50 hours are done sooner.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 1, p. 3; Ohio Revised Code 4507.071 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: During the first 12 months on a probationary license, how many passengers who are not family members may you carry without a parent or guardian?
exp: In the first 12 months, a probationary driver may carry no more than one non-family passenger unless a parent or guardian is along.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 12, p. 47; Ohio Revised Code 4507.071 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: You have held your probationary license for 14 months and are 17. When may you not drive alone without an exception?
exp: After 12 months, the probationary curfew is 1 a.m. to 5 a.m. until you turn 18.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 12, p. 47; Ohio Revised Code 4507.071 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: During the first 12 months of a probationary license, when may you not drive without a parent or guardian, unless an exception applies?
exp: The first year curfew runs from midnight to 6 a.m.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 12, p. 47; Ohio Revised Code 4507.071 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: A 15-year-old TIPIC holder wants to practice. Who may sit in the front passenger seat?
a: A parent, guardian, custodian, licensed driving instructor, or a person 21 or older acting as a parent
c: Any licensed driver 21 or older, even a stranger to the family
exp: Under 16, the supervisor must be a parent, guardian, custodian, licensed instructor, or an adult 21 or older acting in place of a parent.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 1, p. 2; Ohio Revised Code 4507.05 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: Which form does your parent or guardian sign to certify your 50 practice hours?
exp: The notarized BMV 5791 certifies the 50 hours and goes to the driving test and the license purchase.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 12, p. 45; Ohio Revised Code 4507.21(B)(2), (I) (codes.ohio.gov); BMV, Driver License and ID Cards (ohiobmv.gov/dl-gdl.aspx)

q: A probationary driver drives home from a late shift at 1 a.m. in the first year. What must they carry?
exp: Driving to or from work during curfew hours is allowed with employer documentation on form BMV 2825.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 12, p. 47; Ohio Revised Code 4507.071 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: Which form covers a probationary driver going to or from a school or religious event during curfew hours?
exp: Form BMV 2826, signed by the event official, covers official school and religious events.

q: Under Ohio's probationary rules, which phone use is allowed for a 16-year-old driver?
a: Calling for help in an emergency
b: A hands-free call to a parent
c: Reading a text at a red light
d: Talking on speakerphone with the phone in a holder
exp: Drivers under 18 may not use any electronic device while driving, even hands-free; emergency calls and hands-free navigation are the exceptions.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 3, p. 8; Ohio Revised Code 4511.205 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: What is the penalty for a first violation of Ohio's device ban for drivers under 18?
d: A one-year suspension and a $300 fine
exp: A first violation brings a 60-day suspension and a $150 fine; a second brings one year and $300.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 3, p. 8; Ohio Revised Code 4511.205 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: A driver under 18 is convicted of two moving violations. What does the BMV do?
exp: Two moving violations before 18 bring an automatic three-month suspension; three bring one year.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 6, p. 26; Ohio Revised Code 4510.31 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: How long is the automatic suspension when a driver under 18 is convicted of three moving violations?
exp: Three moving violations before 18 lead to an automatic one-year suspension.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 6, p. 26; Ohio Revised Code 4510.31 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: A 16-year-old got a license and, four months later, is convicted of a moving violation. What may the court order?
a: That a parent or guardian ride along for six months or until age 17
b: That the driver retake driver education
d: That the driver hold a TIPIC for one more year
exp: If licensed before 17, a moving violation within six months can lead to court-ordered parent supervision for six months or until 17.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 12, p. 47; Ohio Revised Code 4507.071 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: Which of these does an under-18 driver need before driving again after a probationary suspension?
a: Only payment of the reinstatement fee
b: A new TIPIC, a juvenile driver improvement program and a passed driving test
exp: Reinstatement requires a TIPIC, an approved juvenile driver improvement program and passing the driving examination.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 6, p. 26; Ohio Revised Code 4510.31 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: How many times may you take the Ohio knowledge test online?
exp: Online testing allows two attempts in six months; in person, attempts are unlimited at one per day.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 1, p. 1; BMV, Driver License and ID Cards (ohiobmv.gov/dl-gdl.aspx)

q: You fail the knowledge test at a Driver Exam Station. When can you take it again?
exp: You must wait one day; you may take the test only once a day.

q: What equipment is required to take the Ohio knowledge test online?
a: A computer or laptop with a working webcam
b: A smartphone with the BMV app
d: Any device with an internet browser
exp: Online testing needs a computer or laptop with a webcam; phones and tablets are not allowed.
src: BMV, Driver License and ID Cards (ohiobmv.gov/dl-gdl.aspx)

q: Under 18, who must come with you to buy the TIPIC?
b: A parent or guardian, to co-sign the application
exp: A parent or guardian must be present to co-sign a minor's TIPIC application.

q: Until what age is the parent who co-signs a minor's Ohio license responsible with the minor for damage caused by the minor's driving?
exp: The co-signer is jointly liable until the minor's 18th birthday, unless proof of financial responsibility is filed.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 12, p. 45; Ohio Revised Code 4507.07 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: Which Ohio card can you use alone to board a domestic flight?
exp: The Compliant card meets federal ID rules; a Standard card must be used with a passport or other accepted ID.

q: How many documents proving your Ohio address do you need for a Compliant card?
exp: A Compliant card requires two documents proving your Ohio street address.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 12, p. 46; Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 1, p. 2

q: How much does an Ohio TIPIC cost, including the Deputy Registrar fee?
exp: The BMV fee schedule lists the operator temporary permit at $26.50, Deputy Registrar fee included.

q: What binocular vision lets you get an Ohio license with no daylight-only restriction?
exp: 20/40 or better passes with no restriction; worse than 20/40 up to 20/70 brings daylight-only driving.

q: Your binocular vision measures 20/60. What happens?
c: You must take the test with an eye doctor present
d: You may get a license limited to daylight driving
exp: Vision worse than 20/40 but no worse than 20/70 qualifies for a daytime-only license.

q: Which vehicle class covers an ordinary car, pickup or van in Ohio?
exp: A Class D operator's license covers motor vehicles that need no CDL or endorsement.

q: Under 21, how long must you wait to retake a failed Ohio driving test?
exp: Applicants under 21 must wait two days before retesting.

q: You are 22 and fail the Ohio driving test for the first time. What must you do before your second try?
c: Complete an Abbreviated Adult Driver Training Course, unless you took driver education in the past year
exp: Applicants 21 or older who fail the driving test must complete the abbreviated adult course unless they finished approved driver education within one year.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 11, p. 43 to 44; Ohio Revised Code 4507.21 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: In the Abbreviated Adult Driver Training Course, what follows the 4-hour class if you choose to practice with a licensed adult instead of a driving school?
a: 4 hours of driving with a licensed driver 21 or older
c: 8 hours of driving with any licensed driver
d: 24 hours of driving with a licensed driver 21 or older
exp: The adult option is 24 hours with a licensed driver 21 or older, no more than 4 hours a day, on form BMV 5789.

q: Under the 24-hour practice option of the abbreviated adult course, what is the most you may count in one day?
exp: No more than four hours of driving may be completed in one day.

q: You are 19 and have never had a license. Which Ohio requirement applies to you?
d: None; adults only take the tests
exp: Applicants under 21 need driver education and the 50-hour affidavit; the six-month hold applies only under 18.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 1, p. 3; BMV, Driver License and ID Cards (ohiobmv.gov/dl-gdl.aspx)

q: Once you become an Ohio resident, how soon must you get an Ohio driver license?
exp: Ohio drivers must have an Ohio license within 30 days of establishing residency.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 13, p. 50; BMV, New to Ohio (ohiobmv.gov/new-to-ohio.aspx)

q: You move to Ohio with a valid license from another state. What will the BMV check?
exp: With a valid out-of-state license, the BMV may waive the knowledge and driving tests; a vision screening is required.
src: BMV, New to Ohio; Ohio Revised Code 4507.10 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: A licensed driver from which country can get an Ohio license under a reciprocity agreement without the knowledge and driving tests?
exp: Ohio's reciprocity list includes Canada, France, Germany, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 1, p. 3; Ohio Revised Code 4507.101 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: A temporary resident aged 25 with a license from a country without reciprocity applies for an Ohio license. How long must they hold the TIPIC?
exp: Temporary residents 21 or older need driver education, 50 hours and at least 14 days on the TIPIC.

q: What happens to your Ohio ID card when you are issued a TIPIC?
d: It is mailed back to you later
exp: An Ohio resident may hold only one license or ID card, so the ID card is canceled.

q: What is the speed limit in an Ohio school zone during recess or while children are arriving or leaving?
exp: Ohio's school zone limit is 20 mph during recess and arrival and dismissal times.

q: You are caught speeding in an Ohio construction zone posted with increased penalty signs. What happens to the fine?
c: It is replaced by points only
exp: The court must impose twice the usual fine for speeding in a posted construction zone.
src: Ohio Revised Code 4511.21(P)(3) (codes.ohio.gov); Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 4, p. 12

q: Outside the posted hours and when no children are present, what speed applies in an Ohio school zone?
exp: The 20 mph limit applies during recess and arrival and dismissal times or as signs show; otherwise the normal limit applies.

q: In an Ohio school zone during school hours, driving faster than what speed is a more serious offense than ordinary speeding?
exp: Going over 35 mph in a school zone during recess or arrival and dismissal times is a fourth degree misdemeanor.

q: Using a handheld phone in an Ohio work zone leads to what fine?
exp: Ohio's distracted driving fines are doubled when the violation happens in a work zone.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 3, p. 8; Ohio Revised Code 4511.204 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: You enter an Ohio work zone and no workers are present. What should you do?
a: Drive the normal limit, since the zone is inactive
b: Speed up to clear the zone quickly
c: Use the shoulder to pass slow traffic
d: Slow down anyway, because lanes may be narrow and the pavement rough
exp: The Ohio manual says to reduce speed in a work zone even when no workers are present.

q: What background color do Ohio work zone signs have?
exp: Work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols.

q: In Ohio, when may you turn left on a steady red light?
a: From any left turn lane after a full stop
b: Never; Ohio bans left turns on red
c: Only at intersections with a green arrow sign
d: After a full stop, when turning from a one-way street into a one-way street
exp: Left on red is allowed only from the far left lane of a one-way street onto another one-way street, unless a sign forbids it.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 5, p. 17; Ohio Revised Code 4511.13 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: You face a steady red arrow pointing right in Ohio, and no sign is posted. What must you do?
a: Stop and wait; you may not turn on the red arrow
b: Stop, then turn right when clear
c: Slow down and turn if no one is coming
exp: A steady red arrow means no turn in that direction unless a sign allows turns on the red arrow.

q: Before turning right on a steady red light in Ohio, what must you do?
a: Slow to 5 mph and look left
b: Stop completely and let all crossing traffic and pedestrians clear
c: Wait for the light to turn yellow
exp: A right turn on red requires a complete stop and yielding to all crossing traffic and pedestrians.

q: From which lane may you turn left on red in Ohio, where it is allowed?
a: Any lane of the one-way street
c: The far left lane of the one-way street
exp: Left on red must be made from the extreme left lane of a one-way street onto another one-way street.

q: A sign at an Ohio intersection allows turns on a steady red arrow. What must you still do?
c: Turn in any direction once clear
d: Stop first, then turn only in the direction of the arrow
exp: Where a sign permits it, a driver may turn on the red arrow only after stopping and only as the arrow points.

q: An Ohio school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing. How far from the bus must you stop?
exp: Ohio drivers must stop at least 10 feet from the front or rear of a stopped school bus.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 5, p. 22; Ohio Revised Code 4511.75 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: A school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on a four-lane road, and you are coming toward it from the opposite direction. What must you do?
a: Stop at least 10 feet from the bus
b: Continue with care; only traffic going the bus's direction must stop
c: Stop and wait for the driver to wave you on
exp: On a road with four or more lanes, only traffic moving in the same direction as the bus must stop.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 5, p. 22; Ohio Revised Code 4511.75 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: How close may you follow a fire truck or ambulance responding to an emergency in Ohio?
exp: Ohio law bars following a responding emergency vehicle closer than 500 feet.

q: A stopped Ohio school bus has no stop arm, but its red lights are flashing. What should you do?
a: Pass slowly, since there is no stop arm
b: Stop only if children are visible
d: Stop; you must stop even without a stop arm
exp: The manual says you are still required to stop if the bus has no stop arm.

q: When may you move again after stopping for an Ohio school bus?
a: When the bus begins to move or the bus driver signals you
b: When the last child reaches the sidewalk
d: When the stop arm starts to fold
exp: You stay stopped until the bus starts moving or the bus driver signals motorists to go.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 5, p. 22; Ohio Revised Code 4511.75 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: What is the maximum fine for passing a stopped school bus in Ohio?
exp: A violation carries a fine of up to $500, a court appearance and a possible suspension.

q: When an Ohio school bus shows flashing amber (yellow) lights, what does it mean?
c: The bus is preparing to stop; get ready to stop
exp: Amber lights flash while the bus prepares to stop; drivers need not stop yet but should prepare to.

q: Which stopped vehicle with flashing lights is covered by Ohio's Move Over law?
b: A car with its hazard lights on
exp: Ohio's law covers public safety, emergency, road service, waste collection, highway maintenance and utility commission vehicles.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 9, p. 38; Ohio Revised Code 4511.213 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: You approach a stopped tow truck with flashing lights on a four-lane highway and cannot safely change lanes. What does Ohio law require?
a: Slow down and pass with caution
exp: If a lane change is unsafe, slow down and proceed with caution at a safe speed.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 9, p. 38; Ohio Revised Code 4511.213 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: What happens to the fine for an Ohio Move Over violation?
c: It stays the same as any traffic ticket
d: It is replaced by a warning
exp: The court must impose twice the usual fine for a Move Over violation.

q: An ambulance with lights and siren comes up behind you on an Ohio street. What must you do?
a: Speed up to clear the way
c: Pull to the right edge, clear of any intersection, and stop until it passes
exp: Ohio law requires drivers to move as close as possible to the right edge or curb, clear of intersections, and stop.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 9, p. 38; Ohio Revised Code 4511.45 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: A fire truck with lights and siren approaches from the opposite direction on a divided highway. What must you do?
c: Turn on your hazard lights and stop
d: You are not required to stop
exp: The duty to stop does not apply when the emergency vehicle travels the opposite way on a divided highway.

q: Fire trucks have stopped at a fire on your block. What does Ohio law say about parking?
a: Do not drive into or park in that block unless directed
c: You may park on the opposite side
d: Parking is fine if you stay in the car
exp: Drivers may not drive into or park within the block where fire apparatus has stopped for an alarm.

q: How far before a turn does Ohio require you to start signaling?
exp: Ohio requires a turn signal at least 100 feet before turning.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 5, p. 17; Ohio Revised Code 4511.39 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: In Ohio, you may not make a U-turn on a curve or near a hilltop where other drivers cannot see you within how many feet?
exp: A U-turn is banned where your car cannot be seen within 500 feet by drivers from either direction.

q: You miss your exit on an Ohio freeway. What should you do?
a: Use the median opening to turn around
c: Stop and wait for a gap
d: Go on to the next exit
exp: Take the next exit; median openings are only for emergency and public safety vehicles.

q: Who may use the openings through the median of an Ohio freeway?
b: Any driver who missed an exit
exp: Median openings are for use only by emergency and public safety vehicles.

q: On a road with four or more lanes in Ohio, which lane should you normally drive in?
d: The lane just right of center
exp: Drive in the right lane; use the lane just right of center to pass and to turn left.

q: Besides your turn signal light, how else may you give the required Ohio turn signal?
c: With a hand and arm signal
d: By turning on your hazard lights
exp: The signal may be given with a mechanical signal or the proper hand and arm signal.

q: What is the speed limit on a rural Ohio freeway unless a sign says otherwise?
exp: Rural freeways in Ohio carry a 70 mph limit.

q: What minimum following distance does the Ohio Driver Manual teach?
exp: Keep at least four seconds, or one car length for every 10 mph, behind the vehicle ahead.

q: What is the speed limit on an ordinary street in an Ohio city or village when no sign is posted?
exp: Streets within a municipal corporation have a 25 mph limit.

q: What is the speed limit in an alley within an Ohio city or village?
exp: Alleys within a municipal corporation have a 15 mph limit.

q: What is the default speed limit on an Ohio highway outside a city or village?
exp: Highways outside municipal corporations have a 55 mph limit unless another rule applies.

q: What is the default limit on a state route inside an Ohio town, outside a business district?
exp: State routes or through highways within municipalities outside business districts have a 35 mph limit.

q: How many points does Ohio assess for driving 30 mph or more over the limit?
exp: Speeding 30 mph or more over the limit adds 4 points.

q: On a road posted at 45 mph, how far over the limit can you be before a speeding conviction carries points in Ohio?
exp: Where the limit is under 55 mph, speeding more than 5 mph over adds 2 points.

q: According to the Ohio manual, besides four seconds, what is another way to measure a minimum following distance?
a: Two vehicle lengths at any speed
b: One vehicle length for every 20 mph
c: One vehicle length for every 10 mph
exp: The manual gives one vehicle length for every 10 mph, or four seconds.

q: What following distance does the Ohio manual give behind a motorcycle?
a: Two seconds, since motorcycles stop quickly
d: At least four seconds, more when the road is wet
exp: Allow at least four seconds behind a motorcycle, or more in wet conditions.

q: Ohio law says you may never drive faster than what?
a: A speed that lets you stop within the assured clear distance ahead
b: The speed of the fastest traffic
d: The speed limit plus 5 mph in good weather
exp: Regardless of the posted limit, you must be able to stop within the assured clear distance ahead.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 4, p. 9; Ohio Revised Code 4511.21(A) (codes.ohio.gov)

q: On eastbound I-670 in Columbus, what does a red X over the left shoulder lane mean?
a: The lane is for buses only
b: The lane is open to carpools
c: Slow down but keep using the lane
d: The lane is closed; do not drive in it
exp: The SmartLane is open when a green arrow shows and closed under a red X.
src: ODOT I-670 SmartLane, as reported by ABC6 (abc6onyourside.com), 2019-10

q: Who may use the I-670 SmartLane in Columbus when the green arrow is lit?
b: Only vehicles with two or more people
exp: ODOT says the lane is not restricted by vehicle type or number of riders when open.
src: ODOT I-670 SmartLane, as reported by ABC6 (abc6onyourside.com), 2019-10

q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in Ohio?
exp: Ohio bans stopping or parking within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 5, p. 23; Ohio Revised Code 4511.68 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: In Ohio, you may not park within how many feet of a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal?
exp: Parking is banned within 30 feet of a stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal.

q: When you park parallel to a curb in Ohio, how far from the curb may your wheels be?
exp: Park parallel to and not more than 12 inches from the curb, facing the direction of traffic.

q: How close to the nearest rail of a railroad crossing may you park in Ohio?
exp: Ohio bans parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

q: How close to a crosswalk at an intersection may you park in Ohio?
exp: Parking is banned on a crosswalk and within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 5, p. 23; Ohio Revised Code 4511.68 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: On an Ohio one-way street, where may you park parallel?
b: Within 12 inches of either the right or the left curb
exp: On one-way streets, you may park within 12 inches of the right or left curb.

q: How close to another parked vehicle may you stop or park in Ohio?
exp: Ohio bans stopping or parking within one foot of another parked vehicle.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 5, p. 23; Ohio Revised Code 4511.68 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: How much space must you leave when passing a bicycle in Ohio?
exp: Ohio law treats three feet or more as a safe passing distance from a bicycle.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 9, p. 35; Ohio Revised Code 4511.27 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: In Ohio, you may cross a solid yellow line to pass a slow vehicle only if it is moving slower than what?
exp: You may cross a solid yellow line to pass a slow vehicle going less than half the posted limit, without speeding, when the oncoming lane is clear.

q: While passing a slow-moving vehicle across a solid yellow line in Ohio, how fast may you go?
a: Up to 10 mph over the limit
b: Any speed needed to pass quickly
d: No faster than the speed limit
exp: You may not exceed the speed limit while passing.

q: What does the orange and red triangle on the back of an Ohio farm vehicle tell you?
a: The vehicle travels at less than 25 mph
c: The vehicle is about to turn
d: The vehicle is wider than a lane
exp: The slow-moving vehicle emblem marks a vehicle traveling less than 25 mph.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 9, p. 38; Ohio Revised Code 4511.31 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: Ohio requires headlights whenever you cannot clearly see objects how far ahead?
exp: Lights must be on whenever natural light does not let you see objects clearly 1,000 feet ahead.

q: Your wipers are running because of light rain at noon. What does Ohio law require?
a: Only your parking lights must be on
c: Your hazard lights must be on
exp: Ohio requires headlights any time your windshield wipers are in use because of precipitation.

q: The other driver in your crash had no insurance, and the damage is over $400. Within what time may you file an Ohio Crash Report (BMV 3303)?
exp: The BMV 3303 may be filed within six months when the other party was uninsured and damage exceeded $400 or someone was hurt.

q: Between what times does Ohio require headlights?
a: 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise
d: Only when it is fully dark
exp: Headlights must be on between sunset and sunrise.

q: Which lights does the Ohio manual say to use when driving in fog?
exp: Use low beams, not high beams, in fog.

q: What does Ohio law say about your headlights when another vehicle approaches from ahead?
a: Keep high beams on so the other driver sees you
d: Aim or dim them so the glare does not shine into the other driver's eyes
exp: Ohio law requires that glaring rays not be projected into the eyes of an oncoming driver, and the manual says to dim for approaching traffic.
src: Ohio Revised Code 4513.15 (codes.ohio.gov); Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 7, p. 28

q: In Ohio, when must you show proof of insurance after a crash?
a: When the crash causes more than $400 in property damage
c: Only if police write a ticket
d: Only when the other driver asks
exp: Proof of financial responsibility must be shown when a driver is in a crash causing more than $400 in property damage.

q: You back into an unattended parked car in Ohio. What must you do?
a: Leave if the damage looks minor
b: Report it to police or leave your information at the scene
c: Wait one hour for the owner
exp: With an unattended vehicle, you must report the crash to police or leave the needed information at the scene.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 10, p. 41; Ohio Revised Code 4549.03 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: After an Ohio crash in which someone is hurt, whom does the manual say to notify besides 911?
c: The Ohio State Highway Patrol, the sheriff or local police
exp: Notify the proper authorities: the Highway Patrol, sheriff or local police.

q: Police signal you to pull over in Ohio. Once stopped, what does the Ohio manual tell you to do?
a: Get out and walk toward the officer
b: Keep the engine running in case you must move
c: Unbuckle your belt to reach your papers
d: Shift into park, turn off the engine and lower your window
exp: The manual says to shift to park, turn the ignition off, lower the window and stay in the car with your belt on.

q: You have a weapon in your car when police stop you. What does the Ohio manual say to do?
a: Tell the officer at first contact
c: Hand the weapon to the officer
exp: The manual says to inform the officer upon first contact if you have a weapon in the vehicle.

q: You disagree with a ticket an Ohio officer gives you. What does the manual advise?
a: Refuse to sign and drive away
b: Stay cooperative and contest the ticket in court
c: Argue your case at the roadside
d: Ask the officer for a warning instead
exp: Be cooperative and do not argue; you may contest the ticket in court.

q: At what BAC is a driver under 21 breaking the law in Ohio?
exp: Ohio makes it illegal for a driver under 21 to drive with a BAC of 0.02 or more.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 6, p. 25; Ohio Revised Code 4511.19(B) (codes.ohio.gov)

q: How long is the license suspension for a first refusal of a chemical test after an Ohio OVI arrest?
exp: A first refusal brings a one-year administrative license suspension.

q: A driver 18 or older is caught holding a phone while driving in Ohio for the first time in two years. What penalty applies?
b: Up to a $150 fine and 2 points
c: Up to a $500 fine and a 90-day suspension
exp: A first offense brings up to $150 and 2 points; a distracted driving course can replace the fine and points.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 3, p. 8; Ohio Revised Code 4511.204 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: What BAC limit applies to a commercial driver in Ohio?
exp: Commercial drivers may not drive with a BAC of 0.04 or higher.

q: What does OVI stand for in Ohio?
a: Operating a vehicle while intoxicated by drugs only
exp: Ohio's term for impaired driving is OVI, operating a vehicle while impaired.

q: In Ohio, at what BAC does a first OVI count as a high test with tougher penalties?
exp: A BAC of 0.17 or more brings the higher penalty tier.

q: Within how long after an OVI arrest must the chemical test be given in Ohio?
exp: The chemical test is requested within two hours of the arrest.

q: A driver refuses the chemical test, then is found not guilty of OVI. What happens to the refusal suspension?
exp: The refusal suspension stands even if the driver is acquitted of the OVI charge.

q: How long is the administrative suspension for a first Ohio chemical test of 0.08 or higher?
exp: A first test over the limit brings a three-month (90-day) suspension.

q: With one prior refusal or OVI conviction in 10 years, how long is the suspension for refusing a chemical test?
exp: One prior refusal or OVI conviction raises the refusal suspension to two years.

q: What is the fine range for a first OVI in Ohio?
exp: A first OVI carries a fine of $565 to $1,075.

q: What is the minimum jail sentence for a first Ohio OVI below the high test level, if the driver does not attend an intervention program?
exp: A first OVI brings 3 consecutive days in jail or a 72-hour driver intervention program.

q: How long is the court license suspension for a first OVI conviction in Ohio?
exp: A first OVI brings a suspension of one to three years, with limited privileges or an interlock possible.

q: In Ohio, who may not have an opened container of beer or liquor in a vehicle on a public road?
d: Only the driver, while the car is moving
exp: Ohio's open container ban covers drivers and passengers, moving or stationary, on roads and public parking areas.

q: An Ohio driver aged 19 has a BAC of 0.03. What is this offense called?
b: OVUAC, operating a vehicle after underage alcohol consumption
exp: A driver under 21 with a BAC from 0.02 to below 0.08 commits OVUAC.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 6, p. 25; Ohio Revised Code 4511.19(B) (codes.ohio.gov)

q: An OVUAC can bring a license suspension of how long in Ohio?
exp: OVUAC can lead to a suspension of three months to two years, a remedial course and a new license exam.

q: A 17-year-old is caught with alcohol while riding in a car in Ohio. What happens to their license?
d: It is suspended for 6 months to 1 year
exp: When an offender under 18 was operating or riding in a vehicle, the court must suspend the permit or license for six months to one year.

q: What is the fine for a first offense of using a false ID to buy alcohol in Ohio?
exp: A first violation with a false or altered ID carries a fine of $250 to $1,000.

q: What fine does an adult face in Ohio for furnishing alcohol to someone under 21?
exp: Furnishing alcohol to an underage person carries a fine of $500 to $1,000 and up to six months in jail.

q: Which phone use is legal for an Ohio driver 18 or older while driving?
a: Typing a short text at 20 mph
b: Holding the phone to read directions
c: A hands-free call started with a single touch
d: Watching a video while in slow traffic
exp: Drivers 18 and older may use hands-free features started or stopped with a single touch or swipe.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 3, p. 8; Ohio Revised Code 4511.204 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: What is the most an Ohio driver can be fined for a third hand-held phone offense within two years?
exp: A third or later offense in two years carries up to $500, 4 points and a possible 90-day suspension.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 3, p. 8; Ohio Revised Code 4511.204 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: What can an Ohio driver do after a first hand-held phone offense to avoid the fine and points?
a: Complete a distracted driving safety course
exp: First offenders may take a distracted driving course instead of paying the fine and receiving points.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 3, p. 8; Ohio Revised Code 4511.204 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: What happens when an Ohio driver collects 12 or more points within two years?
exp: Twelve points in two years brings a class D suspension, which lasts six months.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 6, p. 26; Ohio Revised Code 4510.037 (codes.ohio.gov); Ohio Revised Code 4510.02 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: Under Ohio law, a child who is under 4 years old or under 40 pounds must ride in what?
c: A seat belt in the back seat
exp: Children under 4 or under 40 pounds must be secured in a child safety seat that meets federal standards.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 6, p. 27; Ohio Revised Code 4511.81 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: What are Ohio's minimum liability insurance amounts?
c: $25,000 per person, $50,000 per crash for injury, $25,000 property damage
exp: Ohio requires at least $25,000 for one person, $50,000 for two or more, and $25,000 for property damage.

q: At how many points in two years does the Ohio BMV send a warning letter?
exp: Six points within two years triggers a warning letter.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 6, p. 26; Ohio Revised Code 4510.037 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: How many points does a conviction for OVI or leaving the scene of a crash add in Ohio?
exp: Serious offenses such as OVI, hit-skip and fleeing police carry 6 points.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 6, p. 26; Ohio Revised Code 4510.036 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: How many points do most moving violations add in Ohio?
exp: Most moving violations add 2 points.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 6, p. 26; Ohio Revised Code 4510.036 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: How often can an Ohio driver earn a 2-point credit by completing a remedial driving course?
exp: One two-point credit is allowed in any three-year period, up to five in a lifetime.

q: What is an SR-22?
a: A special type of high-risk insurance policy
d: A form showing your insurance meets Ohio's minimum coverage
exp: An SR-22 is not a type of insurance but a form filed with the state as proof of required coverage.

q: What Ohio booster seat rule applies to a 6-year-old who is 4 feet 2 inches tall?
a: The child must ride in a booster seat
b: The child may use a seat belt alone
exp: Children 4 to under 8 must use a booster seat unless they are at least 4 feet 9 inches tall.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 6, p. 27; Ohio Revised Code 4511.81 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: Up to what age must Ohio children be secured by a seat belt or child seat in any seating position?
exp: Children 8 through 15 must be secured with a seat belt or child restraint.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 6, p. 27; Ohio Revised Code 4511.81 (codes.ohio.gov)

q: Which children does the Ohio manual say should ride in the back seat?
exp: Children 12 and younger should sit in the rear seat to avoid airbag injury.

q: What is the fine for a first violation of Ohio's child restraint law?
exp: A first offense is a minor misdemeanor with a fine of $25 to $75.

q: An adult driver in Ohio is not wearing a seat belt. Can police stop the car for that alone?
a: No; adult belt enforcement is secondary
b: Yes; it is a primary offense
exp: Officers may not stop a vehicle solely to check adult belt use.

q: What is the Ohio seat belt fine for a driver?
exp: The fine is $30 for the driver and $20 for a front seat passenger.

q: What minimum tire tread depth does Ohio require?
exp: A tire must have at least 1/16 inch of tread.
src: Ohio Driver Manual (HSY 7607 10/25), Sec. 2, p. 4 to 5

q: During which period are studded tires legal in Ohio?
exp: Studded tires are legal from November 1 through April 15.

q: What share of light must Ohio front side windows let through?
exp: Front side windows must allow 50 percent light transmission, plus or minus 3 percent; the windshield 70 percent.

q: How many points may you lose on each part of the Ohio driving test and still pass?
exp: Applicants may lose up to 25 points in the maneuverability test and up to 25 in the road test.

q: In the Ohio maneuverability test, what is the size of the box formed by the markers?
exp: You drive forward through a 9 by 20 foot course formed by four markers, with a fifth center marker.

q: During the Ohio maneuverability test, which mistake fails you at once?
a: Stopping once to check your position
c: Bumping a marker without moving it
exp: Running over, knocking down or moving a marker is an immediate failure; bumps and stops cost points.

q: In step one of the Ohio maneuverability test, where should you stop?
a: When your rear bumper is even with the center marker
b: When your front bumper passes the last markers
c: When your mirror lines up with the center marker
exp: Drive forward and stop with your rear bumper even with the center marker, parallel to the course.

q: In step two of the Ohio maneuverability test, where should you stop?
a: With your rear bumper even with the center marker
b: With your front bumper even with the two rear markers
c: Outside the box, past the rear markers
exp: Back past the center marker and stop with the front bumper even with the two rear markers.

q: Which item is checked on your car before an Ohio driving test?
a: That the car has a backup camera
b: That the tank is at least half full
c: That both front doors open from inside and outside
d: That the car has an automatic transmission
exp: The inspection checks signals, brake lights, horn, wipers, headlights and that front doors open from both sides.

q: Where can you schedule an Ohio driving test?
d: Online, or in person at a Driver Exam Station
exp: Schedule online or in person at a Driver Exam Station.
